ei.title: 글의 순서 — 필기 재료의 역사와 종이의 승리
ei.subject: 6월 고2 모의고사
ei.lesson: 글의 순서 — 필기 재료의 역사와 종이의 승리

fullPassage: The transition from an oral culture, in which knowledge was handed down through stories, songs, and apprenticeships, to a literate one, based on the written word, was held back for centuries by the lack of suitable writing material. Stone and clay tablets were used, but they were prone to fracture and were bulky and heavy to transport. Wood suffers from splitting and is susceptible to decay. Wall paintings are static and space is limited. The invention of paper, said to be one of the four great inventions of the Chinese, solved these problems, but it wasn't until the Romans replaced the scroll with the codex — or, as we call it now, the book — that the material reached its full potential. That was two thousand years ago, and it is still a dominant form of the written word. That paper, a much softer material than either stone or wood, won out as the guardian of the written word is a remarkable materials story.

questions.passage: The transition from an oral culture, in which knowledge was handed down through stories, songs, and apprenticeships, to a literate one, based on the written word, was held back for centuries by the lack of suitable writing material. Stone and clay tablets were used, but they were prone to fracture and were bulky and heavy to transport. Wood suffers from (A)[splitting / merging] and is susceptible to decay. Wall paintings are static and space is limited. The invention of paper, said to be one of the four great inventions of the Chinese, (B)[solved / worsened] these problems, but it wasn't until the Romans replaced the scroll with the codex — or, as we call it now, the book — that the material reached its full potential. That was two thousand years ago, and it is still a (C)[minor / dominant] form of the written word. That paper, a much softer material than either stone or wood, won out as the guardian of the written word is a remarkable materials story.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: (A) splitting=갈라짐 / merging=합쳐짐 (B) solved=해결했다 / worsened=악화시켰다 (C) dominant=지배적인 / minor=사소한
det.analysis:
✅ ① splitting — solved — dominant ←정답
❌ ② merging — solved — dominant
❌ ③ splitting — worsened — dominant
❌ ④ splitting — solved — minor

✅ splitting — solved — dominant: 나무는 '갈라짐'(splitting)에 시달리고, 종이의 발명이 문제를 '해결했으며'(solved), 종이는 여전히 '지배적인'(dominant) 형태다 ←정답
❌ merging: '합쳐짐'은 나무가 갈라진다는 문맥과 반대
❌ worsened: '악화시켰다'는 문제를 해결했다(solved)는 흐름과 반대
❌ minor: '사소한'은 여전히 널리 쓰이는 dominant 위치에 부적절
det.tip: splitting(갈라짐) ↔ merging(합쳐짐), solved(해결) ↔ worsened(악화), dominant(지배적) ↔ minor(사소한)

questions.passage: The transition from an oral culture, in which knowledge was handed down through stories, songs, and apprenticeships, to a literate one, based on the written word, was held back for centuries by the lack of suitable writing material. Stone and clay tablets were used, but they were prone to fracture and were bulky and heavy to transport. Wood suffers from splitting and is (A)[susceptible / immune] to decay. Wall paintings are static and space is limited. The invention of paper, said to be one of the four great inventions of the Chinese, solved these problems, but it wasn't until the Romans (B)[replaced / preserved] the scroll with the codex — or, as we call it now, the book — that the material reached its full potential. That was two thousand years ago, and it is still a dominant form of the written word. That paper, a much (C)[harder / softer] material than either stone or wood, won out as the guardian of the written word is a remarkable materials story.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: (A) susceptible=취약한 / immune=면역인 (B) replaced=대체했다 / preserved=보존했다 (C) softer=더 부드러운 / harder=더 단단한
det.analysis:
❌ ① immune — replaced — softer
✅ ② susceptible — replaced — softer ←정답
❌ ③ susceptible — preserved — softer
❌ ④ susceptible — replaced — harder

✅ susceptible — replaced — softer: 나무는 부패에 '취약하고'(susceptible), 로마인들이 두루마리를 '대체했으며'(replaced), 종이는 돌·나무보다 '더 부드러운'(softer) 재료다 ←정답
❌ immune: '면역인'은 부패에 취약하다는 문맥과 반대
❌ preserved: '보존했다'는 두루마리를 코덱스로 바꿨다는 replaced와 반대
❌ harder: '더 단단한'은 종이가 더 부드럽다는 softer와 반대
det.tip: susceptible(취약) ↔ immune(면역), replaced(대체) ↔ preserved(보존), softer(부드러운) ↔ harder(단단한)

questions.passage: The transition from an oral culture, in which knowledge was handed down through stories, songs, and apprenticeships, to a literate one, based on the written word, was held back for centuries by the lack of suitable writing material. Stone and clay tablets were used, but they were prone to fracture and were bulky and heavy to transport. Wood suffers from splitting and is susceptible to decay. Wall paintings are static and space is (A)[limited / endless]. The invention of paper, said to be one of the four great inventions of the Chinese, solved these problems, but it wasn't until the Romans replaced the scroll with the codex — or, as we call it now, the book — that the material (B)[lost / reached] its full potential. That was two thousand years ago, and it is still a dominant form of the written word. That paper, a much softer material than either stone or wood, won out as the guardian of the written word is a (C)[remarkable / ordinary] materials story.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: (A) limited=제한된 / endless=끝없는 (B) reached=도달했다 / lost=잃었다 (C) remarkable=주목할 만한 / ordinary=평범한
det.analysis:
❌ ① endless — reached — remarkable
❌ ② limited — lost — remarkable
✅ ③ limited — reached — remarkable ←정답
❌ ④ limited — reached — ordinary

✅ limited — reached — remarkable: 벽화는 공간이 '제한적'(limited)이고, 코덱스가 되어서야 재료가 잠재력에 '도달했으며'(reached), 종이의 승리는 '주목할 만한'(remarkable) 이야기다 ←정답
❌ endless: '끝없는'은 공간이 제한적이라는 벽화 단점과 반대
❌ lost: '잃었다'는 잠재력에 도달했다(reached)는 흐름과 반대
❌ ordinary: '평범한'은 주목할 만하다(remarkable)와 반대
det.tip: limited(제한된) ↔ endless(끝없는), reached(도달) ↔ lost(잃음), remarkable(주목할 만한) ↔ ordinary(평범한)

questions.passage: The transition from an oral culture, in which knowledge was ①<u>handed down</u> through stories, songs, and apprenticeships, to a literate one, based on the written word, was held back for centuries by the lack of suitable writing material. Stone and clay tablets were used, but they were ②<u>immune</u> to fracture and were bulky and heavy to transport. Wood suffers from splitting and is susceptible to decay. Wall paintings are static and space is limited. The ③<u>invention</u> of paper, said to be one of the four great inventions of the Chinese, solved these problems, but it wasn't until the Romans replaced the scroll with the codex — or, as we call it now, the book — that the material reached its full potential. That was two thousand years ago, and it is still a dominant form of the written word. That paper, a much softer material than either stone or wood, won out as the ④<u>guardian</u> of the written word is a remarkable materials story.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ① handed down=전해진 ② immune→prone (부적절) ③ invention=발명 ④ guardian=수호자
det.analysis:
✅ ① handed down: 지식이 이야기·노래로 '전해졌다'(handed down) — 적절
❌ ② immune: 원문은 prone(~하기 쉬운)인데 immune(면역인)으로 교체됨. 돌·점토판은 파손되기 '쉬운' 것이 단점이므로 prone이 맞음 ←정답
✅ ③ invention: 종이의 '발명'(invention) — 적절
✅ ④ guardian: 종이가 문자의 '수호자'(guardian)로 승리 — 적절
det.tip: prone to fracture(파손되기 쉬운). immune(면역인)은 정반대

questions.passage: The transition from an oral culture, in which knowledge was handed down through stories, songs, and apprenticeships, to a literate one, based on the written word, was held back for centuries by the ①<u>abundance</u> of suitable writing material. Stone and clay tablets were used, but they were prone to fracture and were bulky and heavy to transport. Wood suffers from splitting and is susceptible to decay. Wall paintings are ②<u>static</u> and space is limited. The invention of paper, said to be one of the four great inventions of the Chinese, solved these problems, but it wasn't until the Romans replaced the scroll with the ③<u>codex</u> — or, as we call it now, the book — that the material reached its full potential. That was two thousand years ago, and it is still a dominant form of the written word. That paper, a much softer material than either stone or wood, ④<u>won out</u> as the guardian of the written word is a remarkable materials story.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ① abundance→lack (부적절) ② static=고정된 ③ codex=코덱스 ④ won out=승리했다
det.analysis:
❌ ① abundance: 원문은 lack(부족)인데 abundance(풍부)로 교체됨. '적합한 필기 재료의 부족' 때문에 전환이 지체된 것이므로 lack이 맞음 ←정답
✅ ② static: 벽화가 '고정되어'(static) 있다 — 적절
✅ ③ codex: 두루마리를 대체한 '코덱스'(codex) — 적절
✅ ④ won out: 종이가 최종적으로 '승리했다'(won out) — 적절
det.tip: the lack of suitable writing material(적합한 재료의 부족). abundance(풍부)는 정반대

questions.passage: The transition from an oral culture, in which knowledge was handed down through stories, songs, and ①<u>apprenticeships</u>, to a literate one, based on the written word, was held back for centuries by the lack of suitable writing material. Stone and clay tablets were used, but they were prone to fracture and were bulky and heavy to ②<u>transport</u>. Wood suffers from splitting and is susceptible to decay. Wall paintings are static and space is limited. The invention of paper, said to be one of the four great inventions of the Chinese, solved these ③<u>solutions</u>, but it wasn't until the Romans replaced the scroll with the codex — or, as we call it now, the book — that the material reached its full potential. That was two thousand years ago, and it is still a dominant form of the written word. That paper, a much softer material than either stone or wood, won out as the guardian of the written word is a remarkable ④<u>materials story</u>.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ① apprenticeships=도제 제도 ② transport=운반하다 ③ solutions→problems (부적절) ④ materials story=재료 이야기
det.analysis:
✅ ① apprenticeships: 지식이 이야기·노래·'도제 제도'(apprenticeships)로 전해짐 — 적절
✅ ② transport: 석판이 부피 크고 무거워 '운반하기'(transport) 힘듦 — 적절
❌ ③ solutions: 원문은 problems(문제)인데 solutions(해결책)로 교체됨. 종이가 앞선 재료들의 '문제'를 해결했다는 흐름이므로 problems가 맞음 ←정답
✅ ④ materials story: 종이의 승리는 주목할 만한 '재료 이야기'(materials story) — 적절
det.tip: solved these problems(이 문제들을 해결했다). solutions(해결책)를 solve할 수는 없음

questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 로마인들이 ____을(를) 코덱스, 즉 오늘날의 책으로 대체했다.
det.analysis:
❌ ① poster
❌ ② tablet
❌ ③ painting
✅ ④ scroll ←정답

✅ scroll: 로마인들이 대체한 옛 문서 형태는 '두루마리'(scroll)다. 뒤에 codex(=book)로 대체했다고 했으므로 대체된 대상은 두루마리 ←정답
❌ poster: 포스터는 책으로 대체된 문서 형태가 아님
❌ tablet: 석판은 앞 문장에서 이미 다룬 다른 재료라 이 자리에 부적절
❌ painting: 벽화는 두루마리를 대체한 대상이 아님
det.tip: scroll(두루마리): 코덱스(책) 이전의 두루마리형 문서

det.korean: 돌과 점토판은 ____되기 쉽고 부피가 크고 무거워 운반하기 힘들었다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① fracture ←정답
❌ ② comfort
❌ ③ profit
❌ ④ harmony

✅ fracture: 돌·점토판의 단점으로 '파손'(fracture)되기 쉬움이 이어져야 한다. 뒤의 bulky/heavy 같은 단점 나열과 어울린다 ←정답
❌ comfort: 편안함은 단점이 아니라 문맥과 반대
❌ profit: 이익은 재료의 물리적 단점과 무관
❌ harmony: 조화는 단점 나열과 무관
det.tip: prone to fracture(파손되기 쉬운): 돌·점토판의 단점

det.korean: 돌과 ____ 판이 쓰였으나 파손되기 쉬웠다.
det.analysis:
❌ ① glass
✅ ② clay ←정답
❌ ③ plastic
❌ ④ cloud

✅ clay: 돌과 함께 초기 필기 매체로 쓰인 것은 '점토'(clay) 판이다. 파손되기 쉬웠다는 옛 재료의 단점과 이어진다 ←정답
❌ glass: 유리판은 고대 필기 매체로 부적절
❌ plastic: 플라스틱은 시대에 맞지 않음
❌ cloud: 구름은 문맥과 무관
det.tip: Stone and clay tablets(돌과 점토판): 고대 필기 매체

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 <u>transition</u>과 의미가 가장 가까운 것은?

det.korean: transition=전환 / barrier=장벽 / tradition=전통 / shift=변화 / collapse=붕괴
det.analysis:
❌ ① barrier
❌ ② tradition
✅ ③ shift ←정답
❌ ④ collapse

✅ shift: 구술 문화에서 문자 문화로의 '전환(transition)'은 '변화(shift)'와 의미가 같다 ←정답
❌ barrier: 장벽 — 의미 다름
❌ tradition: 전통 — 철자만 비슷할 뿐 의미 다름
❌ collapse: 붕괴 — 의미 다름
det.tip: transition = shift: 한 상태에서 다른 상태로의 변화

det.korean: bulky=부피가 큰 / portable=휴대하기 쉬운 / smooth=매끄러운 / cheap=값싼 / cumbersome=크고 다루기 힘든

questions.passage: The transition from an oral culture, in which knowledge was handed down through stories, songs, and apprenticeships, to a literate one, based on the written word, was <u>held back</u> for centuries by the lack of suitable writing material. Stone and clay tablets were used, but they were prone to fracture and were bulky and heavy to transport. Wood suffers from splitting and is susceptible to decay. Wall paintings are static and space is limited. The invention of paper, said to be one of the four great inventions of the Chinese, solved these problems, but it wasn't until the Romans replaced the scroll with the codex — or, as we call it now, the book — that the material reached its full potential. That was two thousand years ago, and it is still a dominant form of the written word. That paper, a much softer material than either stone or wood, won out as the guardian of the written word is a remarkable materials story.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 <u>held back</u>과 의미가 가장 반대인 것은?

det.korean: held back=지체시킨 / delayed=지연시킨 / advanced=진전시킨 / ignored=무시한 / repeated=반복한
det.analysis:
❌ ① delayed
✅ ② advanced ←정답
❌ ③ ignored
❌ ④ repeated

✅ advanced: '지체시킨(held back)'의 반대는 '진전시킨(advanced)'이다 ←정답
❌ delayed: 지연시킨 — held back과 같은 뜻인 함정
❌ ignored: 무시한 — 의미 축이 달라 반의어 아님
❌ repeated: 반복한 — 의미 축이 달라 반의어 아님
det.tip: held back(지체) ↔ advanced(진전). delayed는 유의어라 오답

det.korean: oral=구술의 / spoken=말로 하는 / verbal=말의 / written=글로 쓴 / traditional=전통적인

❌ ① spoken
❌ ② verbal
✅ ③ written ←정답
❌ ④ traditional

✅ written: '구술의(oral, 말로 전하는)'의 반대는 '글로 쓴(written)'이다. 글 전체가 oral culture ↔ literate/written의 대비다 ←정답

(B) The teacher handed out extra reading <u>material</u> for the students to study before the test.
questions.stem: 다음 (A)와 (B)의 밑줄 친 material의 의미로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: material: (A) (물리적) 재료 (B) (학습) 자료
det.analysis:
❌ ① (A) 자료 — (B) 재료
❌ ② (A) 재료 — (B) 재료
❌ ③ (A) 자료 — (B) 자료
✅ ④ (A) 재료 — (B) 자료 ←정답

✅ (A) 재료 — (B) 자료: (A) writing material은 글을 쓰는 물리적 '재료'이고, (B) reading material은 공부용 '자료(정보)'다 ←정답
❌ (A) 자료 — (B) 재료: 두 뜻이 뒤바뀜
❌ (A) 재료 — (B) 재료: (B)는 물리적 재료가 아니라 학습 자료
❌ (A) 자료 — (B) 자료: (A)는 정보 자료가 아니라 물리적 재료

questions.stem: 다음 영영 정의에 해당하는 단어로 가장 적절한 것은? "the possibility to develop, achieve, or become something in the future"

det.korean: potential=잠재력 / material=재료 / invention=발명 / tradition=전통
det.analysis:
✅ ① potential ←정답
❌ ② material
❌ ③ invention
❌ ④ tradition

✅ potential: '미래에 발전하거나 무언가가 될 가능성' → 잠재력(potential) ←정답. 본문 reached its full potential 참고
❌ material: 재료 — 정의와 무관
❌ invention: 발명 — 정의와 다름
❌ tradition: 전통 — 정의와 무관
det.tip: the possibility to develop in the future(미래 발전 가능성) = potential(잠재력)

questions.passage: The transition from an oral culture, in which __________ (know) was handed down through stories, songs, and apprenticeships, to a literate one, based on the written word, was held back for centuries. Stone and clay tablets were used, but they were prone to fracture.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 (1단어) (영어로) 쓰시오.

det.korean: know(알다, 동사) → knowledge(지식, 명사). 뒤의 was handed down의 주어 자리이므로 명사가 와야 한다.
det.analysis: know(동사)를 명사 knowledge로 바꿔요. 'in which ___ was handed down'에서 빈칸은 was handed down(전해졌다)의 주어 자리라서 동사가 아니라 명사가 와야 해요. 동사 know에 -ledge를 붙인 명사 knowledge(지식)가 정답이에요.
det.tip: 동사 → 명사: know → knowledge (주어 자리)

❌ failed to survive over time: 시간이 지나 사라졌다 — 여전히 dominant라는 내용과 반대
